Now let $\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)$ be the ideal of $y_{n}(\sigma)$ generated by

$\widecheck{e}_{a,i,j}^{(r)},\check{d}_{b,h,k}^{(s)}$

for all admissible $a,i,j,b,h,k,r,s$. Also write $\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}:=\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)\cap y_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}$. By [To23, Lemma 2.2] we see that $R(^{\nu}y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)=^{\nu}y_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}/^{\nu}\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}$ is Poisson generated by elements

$\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{rcl}&&\widehat{e}_{a,i,j}^{(r)}+\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}\text{ for }a=1,...,m-1,\ 1\leq i\leq\nu_{a},\ 1\leq j\leq\nu_{a+1},\ s_{a,a+1}
with Poisson brackets induced by the bracket on  $y_{n}(\sigma)$ . We will write  $\theta_{a,i,j}^{(r)}$ ,  $\eta_{a,i,j}^{(r)}$  for  $\widehat{e}_{a,i,j}^{(r)}+\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}$  and  $\widehat{d}_{a,i,j}^{(r)}+\widecheck{y}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau}$  . Furthermore  $R(^{\nu}y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)$  is generated as a commutative algebra by elements
$\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{rcl}&&\theta_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)}\text{ for }1\leq a
where  $\theta_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)}:=e_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)}+(\beta)^{i+j}(-1)^{r+s_{a,b}}f_{a,j^{\prime},b,i^{\prime}}^{(r)}$ . Using an inductive argument and (5.49) we see the elements  $\theta_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)}$  can also be defined via the following recursion for all admissible  $a,b,i,j,r$ .
$\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{rcl}&&\theta_{a,i,a+1,j}^{(r)}:=\theta_{a,i,j}^{(r)}\\
&&\theta_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)}:=\{\theta_{a,i,b-1,,k}^{(r-s_{b-1,b})},\theta_{b-1,k,b,j}^{(s_{b-1,b}+1)}\}\end{array}$

Thanks to Theorem 5.6 we see that $R(y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)$ comes equipped with the canonical grading $R(y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)=\bigoplus_{i\geq 0}R(y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)_{i}$ which places $\eta_{a,i,j}^{(r)},\theta_{a,i,j}^{(r)}$ in degree $r$ and the Poisson bracket in degree $-1$. Another crucial feature is the loop filtration $R(y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)=\bigcup_{i\geq 0}\operatorname{F}_{i}R(y_{n}(\sigma),\tau)$ which places $\eta_{a,i,j}^{(r)},\theta_{a,i,j}^{(r)}$ in degree $r-1$ and the bracket in degree $0$. Both of these structures are naturally inherited from $y_{n}(\sigma)$.

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and Slodowy slices in classical Lie algebras
paper.abstract: In this paper we introduce the shifted twisted Yangian of type {\sf AI}, following the work of Lu--Wang--Zhang, and we study their semiclassical limits, a class of Poisson algebras. We demonstrate that they coincide with the Dirac reductions of the semiclassical shifted Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_n$. We deduce that these shifted twisted Yangians admit truncations which are isomorphic to Slodowy slices for many non-rectangular nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}. As a direct consequence we obtain parabolic presentations of the semiclassical shifted twisted Yangian, analogous to those introduced by Brundan--Kleshchev for the Yangian of type {\sf A}. Finally we give Poisson presentations of Slodowy slices for all even nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}, generalising the recent work of the second author.
